name: Noetix Bumi
description: Ultra-low-cost humanoid from Chinese startup Noetix Robotics, aimed squarely at education and home use. Announced at under $1,400 — among the cheapest bipedal humanoids to reach market.
sourcing: Specs sourced from TechNode's and Interesting Engineering's coverage of Noetix's October 2025 announcement, as of September 2026. robotindex does not sell this product — pricing and availability are per Noetix's own preorder terms and third-party retailers, and may vary by region.

pricing.summary: **¥9,998 (~$1,370)** at announcement — among the cheapest full bipedal humanoids on the market. Preorders opened around China's Nov–Dec 2025 shopping festivals; by 2026 it's listed as available through JD.com and a handful of international resellers, though robotindex hasn't independently confirmed direct-to-consumer shipping outside China.

editorial.heading: Sensors & Hardware
editorial.body: Built with **lightweight composite materials** and a self-developed motion control system to hit its price point. Noetix has published limited technical detail beyond battery and dimensions — no official DOF count, camera specs, or compute hardware has been disclosed. The robot ships with an **open programming interface**, alongside a drag-and-drop graphical tool for younger users.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: Announced at ¥9,998 (~$1,370), Bumi is among the cheapest full bipedal humanoids to reach market, per TechNode and Interesting Engineering's coverage of its October 2025 announcement — a concrete price point that meaningfully undercuts most category peers. Noetix has disclosed no official DOF count, camera specs, or compute hardware to contextualize that price.

firmwareCommunity.note: No public SDK or firmware repository has been released. Noetix provides its own graphical programming tool instead. Not currently listed in Builds & Mods.
